Lunica How do I edit, compile, run, and inspect a model? Libraries Where do packages and the standard library come from? Experiments How do I sweep parameters and compare trajectories?

docs.title: Practical rules
docs.text:
• Put equations and state in Modelica.
  • Put discrete decisions, mission phases, and event responses in Rhai.
  • Declare every value another component consumes as a USD outputs: property.
  • Keep parameters in the model or the manifest, not in a hidden script.
  • Recompile after changing a model; the scene runs the compiled artifact.
  • Prefer a small, composable model over one class that knows the whole scene.

docs.title: Cosimulation
docs.text:
Cosimulation is the contract between a Modelica model and the rest of the world. The model advances in its own solver; physics advances in Avian; the master clock decides when the two exchange values. Neither side reaches into the other's state.

LunCoSim implements an FMI-CS-shaped master algorithm. It is not a claim that every participant is an FMI implementation. The native Modelica worker and the FMI 3 Co-Simulation backend share the same master invariants.

docs.title: The master loop
docs.text:
At every fixed step:

  1. The master clock reaches a communication point.
  2. Each due participant receives an input snapshot.
  3. The participant advances by one communication step.
  4. The master waits for every due participant to return.
  5. Validated outputs are published with zero-order hold.
  6. Connections propagate the new values.
  7. Physics and rendering observe the result.

The loop is a data-plane system. It runs directly in FixedUpdate; it is not driven through the typed command bus. A command per tick would put a request id, a dispatch, and a result record in the hot loop for no benefit.

Commands own the control plane: load a scene, compile a model, start or pause a run, change time warp. They start and configure the loop; they do not advance it.

docs.title: Communication points and hold
docs.text:
A communication point is the only time at which values cross the boundary. Between points, the last validated outputs are held. This is the zero-order hold that makes a coupled step deterministic: every consumer sees the same value for the whole interval, regardless of when it reads.

The default running communication interval is one master physics tick. Longer integer tick multiples are explicit multirate settings. Each worker request admits its ordered input vector atomically, and the shared clock waits for the complete validated response.

A participant that misses its step budget does not silently return a stale value. The step fails visibly, the coupled step faults, and the simulation holds.

docs.title: Participants and ports
docs.text:
A participant is a SimComponent with named inputs and outputs. Its interface is published from the model's declaration, not from its solution:

Modelica class
  input Real throttle;
  output Real speed;
        │
        ▼
USD component prim
  float inputs:throttle
  float outputs:speed
        │
        ▼
PortRegistry
  declared names, types, units, bounds, owner

This ordering matters. A model that has not produced a sample yet still has an interface. Admission can check the wire, the units, and the initial inputs before the solver has run.

A model output becomes externally connectable only when the component prim declares the matching outputs:<name> property. The runtime does not expose private local variables as public ports.

docs.title: Initial admission
docs.text:
Initialization is not "step from zero and hope." The owner separates declaration, numerical admission, and running exchange:

  1. Source interfaces and native physical definitions become available.
  2. Acyclic participants initialize from finite producer samples.
  3. Participants with complete inputs prepare independently.
  4. Coupled participants are captured into a composite initialization problem.
  5. The composite is compiled and solved at one physical coordinate.
  6. Members are released together only after their observations agree within solver tolerance.

The synth.coupled-initialization hook emits the composite. Rust supplies the member facts, classes, bindings, and probes; Rhai emits the nested array literals in their checked order. Participant parameter values travel separately as qualified Initialize.parameter_overrides names such as p0.k or p0.gains[2].

A missing required free coordinate is an error, including an explicitly empty supplied inventory. Failed certification reports a terminal runtime fault and holds the affected participants. A changed source or wire cannot release an old certificate.

This follows FMI 3.0's separation of Initialization Mode and running communication: initialization loops are solved at one physical coordinate before participants advance.

docs.title: Modelica output ownership
docs.text:
Modelica publishes outputs through its worker response path. The response bridge validates the session, step identity, and communication endpoint before taking the in-flight transaction. Session IDs fence stale results: when a compile or parameter update bumps the session, an in-flight step for the old session is discarded.

The worker reuses immutable compiled DAE artifacts for the same exact target, document URI, assembled source bytes, and source-root revision. Parameter bindings, solver instances, live state, and telemetry remain per entity.

A live solver step failure keeps the solver error and lists the Modelica values that were not produced by the failed step. The list includes each value's last accepted sample and the sample and communication-target times. Names are sorted for stable diagnostics.

docs.title: Backend registry
docs.text:
Backends self-register at application boot. Each domain crate installs a Bevy plugin that inserts itself into BackendRegistry. Dropping a crate removes its backend. A scenario that references a missing backend fails gracefully at load.

Current backends include:

Backend Source Notes Modelica .mo Rumoca worker Rhai .rhai Scripted participant Python .py Optional feature FMI 3 CS .fmu Native import, scalar Float64 profile Avian USD physics Typed-port participant

The FMI adapter uses the existing port and connection boundary. It loads and validates modelDescription.xml, preserves value references and scalar engineering contracts, and runs the FMI 3 Co-Simulation lifecycle on its native worker.

docs.title: The FMI boundary
docs.text:
The native profile supports scalar Float64 ports. Unit and range projection are implemented, and the shared connection fabric compiles compatible unit conversions. The importer declines Event Mode and early return; FMUs handle their internal events. lastSuccessfulTime must match the requested communication point within the timestamp tolerance.

FMI permits lastSuccessfulTime to deviate from the requested endpoint even when earlyReturn is false. The owner faults such a response because the current master cannot synchronize all participants at the reported time. Supporting intermediate communication points would require rescheduling the complete due participant set.

FMI Model Exchange requires a separate solver integration and is not admitted as an FMI-CS participant. Other types, arrays, Scheduled Execution clocks, and externally hosted FMUs are rejected with owner diagnostics.

This is an FMI-CS-shaped master, not a broad conformance claim. FMU-to-FMU unit conversion, implicit coupling, and full FMI conformance require separate qualification.

docs.title: Pause, time warp, and health
docs.text:
Pausing stops the master clock without tearing down participants. A paused model retains its state and its last outputs. Resuming continues from the same communication point.

Time warp changes how fast wall-clock time advances relative to simulation time. It does not change the communication contract: the master still waits for every due participant at each point.

Modelica execution publishes a scene-scoped ModelicaHealthSnapshot from the admitted step counters. Its one-second native wall-clock window reports completed-step FPS and worker service time through the shared engine-health exposure. This diagnostic math does not change simulation scheduling.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
A rover has a Modelica drivetrain, an Avian chassis, and a Rhai mission:

Rhai mission
  └─ SetPorts { throttle, steer }
        └─ Controller.inputs:throttle / inputs:steer
              └─ Modelica Drive
                    └─ outputs:left_torque / outputs:right_torque
                          └─ Chassis.inputs:left_torque / inputs:right_torque
                                └─ Avian wheel torques

At each fixed step:

  1. The mission's latest command is already latched in the port registry.
  2. The controller receives throttle and steer.
  3. The solver advances and returns the two torques.
  4. The torques propagate to the chassis inputs.
  5. Avian applies them to the wheels.
  6. The next step samples the new chassis state.

The mission does not step the controller. The controller does not read the scene. The chassis does not know which language produced the torque.

docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Treat the fixed step as the only exchange point.
  • Declare the interface before relying on a sample.
  • Expect a missing initial input to hold admission, not to become zero.
  • Keep continuous behavior in Modelica; keep discrete decisions in Rhai.
  • Use multirate only when a participant genuinely needs a slower clock.
  • Inspect CausalTrace when a value does not arrive where the wire says it should.
  • Do not claim FMI conformance beyond the tested scalar profile.

Continue with Lunica, the workbench for authoring and running these models.

docs.title: Experiments
docs.text:
An experiment is one run of a compiled model over an explicit time horizon, with its own parameter overrides, inputs, solver bounds, status, and result. The experiments framework exists so that a model can be run many times for parametric study, regression checks, and comparison, without editing the model source between runs.

LunCoSim has two execution modes for Modelica. Live cosimulation advances a model at wall-clock pace alongside the scene, physics, and other participants. Fast Run executes a model from t_start to t_end as quickly as the machine allows and retains the trajectory. Experiments are the second mode. The two modes share the compiler and the model source, but not the run lifecycle.

docs.title: Why experiments are first-class objects
docs.text:
A result file keyed only by model name forces the user to manage filenames and to remember which parameter set produced which curve. An experiment instead carries its own definition next to its result: overrides, inputs, bounds, status, and trajectory travel together. The comparison view is therefore the default view, not a separate tool that opens several files.

The framework is backend-agnostic. The current execution backend is Rumoca with the diffsol solver. The Experiment and RunResult types do not depend on Modelica, so an FMU-backed, code-generated, hardware-in-the-loop, or remote worker backend can be added without changing the registry or the plots.

docs.title: The experiment record
docs.text:
An experiment belongs to a Twin and names an opaque model reference:

Experiment
  id             stable UUID
  twin_id        owning Twin
  model_ref      backend-owned reference to the compiled model
  name           editable display name, initially "<model> — N"
  overrides      parameter path -> typed value
  inputs         input path -> typed value
  bounds         run horizon and solver options
  status         Pending, Queued, Running, Done, Failed, Cancelled
  result         retained trajectory, once complete
  created_at     creation time
  color_hint     stable plot color

Overrides and inputs are ordered maps keyed by a dotted Modelica path such as rocket.engine.thrust. Values are typed: Real, Int, Bool, String, Enum, or RealArray. A parameter with a non-literal binding is shown in the override editor as unsupported; the first version does not rewrite expressions or records.

The run bounds are:

Field Meaning t_start First time point t_end Last time point; must be strictly greater than t_start dt Output interval; omitted means a derived grid n_intervals Output interval count; takes precedence over dt tolerance Solver tolerance solver Registered solver demand h0 Initial step hint

Bounds are validated before registration, before scheduler admission, and again at the shared native/browser execution boundary. The horizon must be finite and strictly increasing. Explicit dt, tolerance, and h0 must be finite and positive. An interval count must be positive and at most 200,000 intervals (200,001 inclusive points). The runner never silently enlarges an explicit interval.

The model's own annotation supplies defaults when the experiment does not. An explicit Interval annotation takes precedence over NumberOfIntervals. With no annotation, the Modelica default of 500 intervals applies. An invalid annotation is a visible failure, not an implicit substitution.

docs.title: Running an experiment
docs.text:
A Fast Run compiles the model once, admits the requested output grid, and then executes the immutable compiled artifact with the experiment's parameter and input values. The compiled artifact is not mutated per run and the source is not reflattened for every point. Unsupported bindings are reported as run errors at the runner boundary.

The run is asynchronous. The registry marks the row Queued before dispatch, then Running with a current time, and finally Done with a wall-clock duration, Failed with a diagnostic, or Cancelled. Progress is throttled to roughly 10 Hz. Cancellation is polled between solver steps and is available for queued and running rows.

A completed result contains:

RunResult
  times    monotonically nondecreasing time samples
  series   dotted variable path -> samples
  meta     units, descriptions, and run facts

Equal timestamps are valid: a solver event can produce distinct pre-event and post-event values at the same time. The result is stored as one immutable Arc, so readers capture the exact completed trajectory without copying its series. A failed run publishes its diagnostic without a trajectory.

The registry retains at most 20 terminal runs per Twin. Pending, queued, and running rows are not evicted. The completed-run channel uses the scalar budget captured at admission, so a later settings change cannot alter an in-flight result boundary. The default result limits are 8,000,000 scalar values and 256 MiB of artifact bytes. A budget failure is a terminal Failed state and releases the scheduler slot.

docs.title: The Experiments panel
docs.text:
The Modelica workbench exposes two run controls:

[ Interactive ▶ ]   [ Fast ⏩  0 → 10 s, dt = auto ⚙ ]

The bounds shown beside Fast come from the current document annotation, or from the documented defaults when the annotation supplies no horizon. The gear opens the override editor.

The Experiments dock lists the retained runs:

☑ ● rocket — 1     0..10 s   Done       1.2 s
☑ ● rocket — 2     0..10 s   Done       1.3 s
☐ ● rocket — 3     0..30 s   Failed       ⓘ
☑ ● rocket — 4     0..10 s   ▮▮▮▮▱▱ 4.2 s

The checkbox toggles plot visibility. The color dot is locked to the run id. Loading or rerunning a row requires its pinned source document and runtime owner to remain active; its overrides and bounds apply only to that document's model draft. The row shows Queued when the scheduler is full; the Run button queues work rather than disabling.

The Graphs panel uses one variable picker across experiments. Each selected variable plots once per checked run, and the legend reads <experiment> · <variable path>. The plot renderer is shared with the live trajectory view. It supports log-Y, fit/reset, overlays, and scrubbing. Long series are min-max decimated to about one sample per display point before drawing, which preserves narrow peaks.

docs.title: Parallel execution
docs.text:
A sweep runs several points at once under one bounded scheduler. Two mechanisms make this efficient and both are part of the current implementation.

Compile once, sweep many. Batch and live compilation share admitted source roots and a bounded compiled-artifact cache keyed by the exact target, document URI, source bytes, and library generation. The runner applies parameter overrides and initial inputs to the compiled model without reflattening it per point. Browser batches compile in the Modelica Web Worker.

Per-run demultiplexing. Results route by exact run id and admitted origin. Native runs use one channel per run handle; the browser build uses a run-id map in the worker transport. Cancellation is per run.

max_parallel bounds the whole scheduler, not one model. The defaults are:

Platform Primitive Default cap Native One thread per run available_parallelism() - 1, clamped to 1–4 Browser Persistent worker pool Auto is 1; the pool is clamped to at most 8 workers

Worker 0 is the primary for parse, compile, and source-library traffic. Every worker, including worker 0, can execute a Fast Run; dispatch prefers a free non-primary worker and falls back to worker 0 only when the others are busy.

The native spawn is fallible. A worker panic becomes a terminal Failed diagnostic, and the completion guard releases the scheduling slot on every exit. A poisoned compiler fails subsequent compilation visibly. Cancelling a queued job withdraws it immediately; cancelling a running job prevents trajectory publication. Closing a Twin cancels that owner's queued and executing runs.

The cap is global and deliberately modest: each concurrent run holds its own result buffers and DAE clone, and the browser additionally holds an MSL copy per worker. Changing the cap at runtime on the web build requires a page reload to resize the fixed pool.

docs.title: Durable history
docs.text:
Completed runs can be persisted as optional artifacts next to the Twin. The artifact adapter captures the exact runtime owner, storage root, result limits, immutable definition, and trajectory. A durable write announces a new manifest only after storage reports success. Application runs have no Twin artifact destination.

The persisted envelope is versioned JSON. It does not store raw workspace Twin IDs or filesystem roots. A compiler-owned content identifier describes the successful strict target and the participating source contributions before user overlays are cleared; host paths and mount identifiers do not contribute. Parsed library records retain their exact source text, so participating library bytes contribute to the identifier while unused libraries do not.

Storage lists at most the registry's 20 retained entries and reads each candidate under the captured byte cap. A malformed or missing optional history warns without failing authored loading or a valid run. Rehydration uses the same bounded registry, an explicit archived runtime origin, and restored_history metadata; it emits no live completion or playback. An archived trajectory is queryable without pretending it came from the currently edited document.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
A run is reproducible when its inputs are fixed:

  • the model source and every library that contributes to the compile;
  • the exact target and compiler build;
  • parameter overrides, inputs, and initial values;
  • bounds, tolerance, solver, and initial step;
  • the result limits, which determine whether a run completes or fails.

The artifact content identifier covers the compiled target and participating sources. It does not cover presentation metadata such as the experiment name or color, which may change without invalidating history.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text: Limit Consequence One global max_parallel A large sweep and a small sweep share the same bound Cold cache race Two cache-miss runs of one model can compile the same DAE concurrently; the duplicate work is harmless Memory N concurrent runs hold N result buffers and N DAE clones Registry cap At most 20 terminal runs per Twin are retained Override scope Inherited, expression-bound, array, and record parameters are not overridable in the first version Browser pool A runtime cap change needs a page reload No parameter grid UI A sweep is currently defined by individual experiment rows

docs.title: Relation to live cosimulation
docs.text:
Experiments do not replace live cosimulation. A live participant keeps a persistent session and exchanges values at communication points; an experiment compiles, runs to completion, and retains a trajectory. A model can be exercised in both modes, but an experiment result is not a live scene state and cannot be possessed or wired into physics. Use live cosimulation to inspect behavior in the scene and experiments to compare many parameter sets quickly.

Continue with Rhai, which owns mission sequencing and the policy that reacts to simulation state.

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
Modelica is a declarative, equation-based language. A class describes relationships that must hold at every instant; the solver decides how to advance them. This is the opposite of a script, where the author decides the order of assignments.

This section covers the language surface LunCoSim authors use most. It is not a replacement for the Modelica specification. The compiler is the authority: a construct that Rumoca does not support fails at compile time, and the failure names the source location.

docs.title: A class is a namespace and a contract
docs.text:
within LunarBase.Power;

model Battery
  parameter Real capacity_wh = 1000;
  parameter Real nominal_voltage = 28;
  Real state_of_charge(start = 1.0);
  output Real voltage;
  input Real current;
equation
  voltage = nominal_voltage * (0.9 + 0.1 * state_of_charge);
  der(state_of_charge) = -current / (capacity_wh / nominal_voltage) / 3600;
end Battery;
Part Meaning within LunarBase.Power; The enclosing package model Battery A reusable class parameter Constant during a run; tunable between runs Real state_of_charge(start = 1.0) A continuous state with an initial guess output Part of the external interface equation A relationship that must hold

The start attribute is a guess, not an initial equation. Use initial equation when the initial value is a constraint.

docs.title: Class kinds
docs.text:
Kind Purpose model A general behavioral model block A model with a fixed input/output interface connector An interface point for acausal connections record A structured value with named fields function An algorithm with inputs and one output package A namespace for other classes type A constrained scalar type class The general form; the others are restrictions

Most LunCoSim assets use model, connector, record, and package. A block is useful when the direction of every boundary variable is known.

docs.title: Built-in types and arrays
Variability and causality
docs.text:
Prefix Meaning parameter Constant during a run, settable between runs constant Fixed at compile time discrete Changes only at events input Supplied by the surrounding system output Exposed to the surrounding system flow A conserved quantity through a connector

A variable with none of these is a local continuous variable. It may still be readable as an observable, but it is not writable from USD.

docs.title: Equations
docs.text:
An equation section contains equalities, not assignments:

equation
  v = i * r;
  der(q) = i;

The solver may solve for either side. This is what makes acausal connectors work: a connector does not say "this is an input"; the equations decide.

An initial equation section constrains the initial state:

initial equation
  q = 0;
  der(q) = 0;

An algorithm section is imperative and is used for discrete logic or functions. It is not a substitute for an equation section when a continuous relationship is intended.

docs.title: Connectors and acausal connections
docs.text:
A connector declares the variables that cross a boundary:

connector HydraulicPort
  flow Real m_flow;
  Real pressure;
end HydraulicPort;

model Pipe
  HydraulicPort inlet;
  HydraulicPort outlet;
equation
  inlet.m_flow + outlet.m_flow = 0;
  outlet.pressure = inlet.pressure - 1000 * inlet.m_flow;
end Pipe;

Two connectors are joined with connect:

model Circuit
  Pipe pipe;
  Tank tank;
equation
  connect(tank.outlet, pipe.inlet);
end Circuit;

connect generates the equality and conservation equations for the connected variables. It is not a signal wire in the USD sense. USD connectors: exposes the acausal interface on a component boundary; USD inputs: and outputs: are causal.

docs.title: Events and discrete behavior
docs.text:
Modelica handles discrete changes with when:

model Thermostat
  input Real temperature;
  output Boolean heater;
  parameter Real threshold = 20.0;
equation
  heater = temperature < threshold;
end Thermostat;

model Counter
  discrete Integer count(start = 0);
equation
  when sample(0, 1.0) then
    count = pre(count) + 1;
  end when;
end Counter;
Operator Meaning when condition then ... end when Execute equations at an event pre(x) The value of x immediately before the event edge(x) True when x changes from false to true change(x) True when x changes reinit(x, value) Reset a state at an event sample(start, interval) A periodic event

Use when for discrete state. Do not emulate a mission phase machine with continuous equations; that belongs in Rhai.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
A function is an algorithm with typed inputs and one output:

function saturate
  input Real value;
  input Real limit;
  output Real result;
algorithm
  result := max(-limit, min(limit, value));
end saturate;

Functions are useful for reusable math and for expressions that would otherwise be repeated. They do not own state.

docs.title: Packages and lookup
docs.text:
A package groups classes:

within LunarBase;

package Power
  model Battery
    // ...
  end Battery;

  model SolarArray
    // ...
  end SolarArray;
end Power;

A class is identified by its qualified name, LunarBase.Power.Battery. The within clause establishes the enclosing scope. Imports shorten lookup:

within LunarBase;

model Rover
  import Modelica.Blocks.Math;
  Math.Max maxBlock;
end Rover;

The compiler resolves the full closure from the admitted source roots. A missing package or class is a compile error, not an empty declaration.

docs.title: Inheritance and modifications
docs.text:
extends applies a base class and can modify its parameters:

model LargeBattery
  extends Battery(capacity_wh = 4000);
end LargeBattery;

Inheritance is resolved before the class's own declarations. Missing bases and inheritance cycles are rejected. A modification changes a parameter default or a nested declaration; it does not create a second equation system.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text:
Annotations carry presentation and experiment metadata:

model Drive
  annotation(
    experiment(StartTime = 0, StopTime = 10, Tolerance = 1e-6),
    Icon(graphics = {Rectangle(extent = {{-100, -100}, {100, 100}})})
  );
end Drive;
Annotation Used by Icon Diagram and component palette Diagram Authored placement and connections experiment Fast Run default bounds Documentation Class documentation panel

An invalid annotation is a diagnostic, not a reason to drop the model. The diagram editor projects the authored placement when present and a deterministic grid when it is not.

docs.title: Source encoding
docs.text: The parser accepts a single leading UTF-8 BOM and retains source coordinates in the original text. Loaders, documents, and editor paste preserve the authored bytes. The production modelica_source_encoding.rhai gate verifies exact text, batch output, and a parser-owned negative diagnostic for the current source generation.

docs.title: What the compiler rejects
docs.text:
Rumoca is strict about the constructs it supports. The following are rejected rather than approximated:

  • missing or cyclic type information;
  • unresolved base classes;
  • malformed or unbalanced models;
  • indexed structural overrides that the root-modifier owner cannot represent;
  • aggregate, array, or string values where a scalar run value is required;
  • non-finite numeric admission.

A rejected model is a visible compile diagnostic. The runtime does not fall back to a stale artifact or a default model.

docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Prefer equations over algorithms for continuous behavior.
  • Use initial equation for constraints and start for guesses.
  • Use connectors for physical conservation; use input/output for signal boundaries.
  • Keep discrete mission logic out of Modelica.
  • Qualify names with packages; do not rely on a flat global namespace.
  • Treat a compile diagnostic as the source of truth.

Continue with Cosimulation, where these equations meet the fixed-step clock.

docs.title: Libraries
docs.text:
A Modelica library is a package tree of reusable classes. LunCoSim admits source roots, resolves qualified names through them, and compiles the reachable closure. The Package Browser and the compiler read the same source-root inventory.

Libraries are ordinary .mo files with package.mo and package.order structure. There is no LunCoSim-specific package format.

docs.title: The standard library
docs.text:
The engine ships the Modelica Standard Library (MSL) and the DLR Thermofluid Stream library as downloadable assets. Their manifest is assets/manifests/modelica.toml:

[library]
name = "Modelica Standard Library"
version = "4.1.0"
url = "https://github.com/modelica/ModelicaStandardLibrary/archive/refs/tags/v4.1.0.tar.gz"
dest = "library"

[thermofluidstream]
name = "DLR Thermofluid Stream Library"
version = "1.3.0"
url = "https://github.com/DLR-SR/ThermofluidStream/archive/refs/tags/v1.3.0.tar.gz"
dest = "thermofluidstream"

The libraries are not downloaded in the background on launch. A missing library is shown in Settings → Data & libraries and starts downloading only after an explicit request.

A Twin can also use the application's packaged source bundle:

[modelica]
externals = [
  { name = "BundledModelicaLibraries", path = "@bundled:source-bundle" },
]

@bundled:source-bundle is owned by the bundled source-library inventory, not by a Twin folder. It is always available and is admitted lazily on first compile.

docs.title: Source roots
docs.text:
[modelica].paths lists Twin-relative search roots:

[modelica]
paths = ["models", "shared"]

A path may be "." to make the Twin root a search root. The default is ["."].

[modelica].externals adds libraries outside the Twin:

[modelica]
externals = [
  { name = "BundledModelicaLibraries", path = "@bundled:source-bundle" },
  { name = "MyPkg", path = "../shared_library/" },
]

Relative paths work for sibling-folder libraries in a monorepo. Absolute paths are supported but break portability; the editor warns on save. A git URL form is not part of the current contract.

The authored twin.lifecycle policy selects which roots to load. Rust validates the Twin-scoped path, registers the generic source root, and sends it through the worker. The worker recursively reads package.mo and package.order trees and uses the same input-default normalization as other disk roots.

docs.title: Package structure
docs.text:
A package is a directory with a package.mo:

models/
  LunarBase/
    package.mo
    package.order
    Power/
      package.mo
      package.order
      Battery.mo
      SolarArray.mo

package.mo declares the package:

within;
package LunarBase
  annotation(
    Documentation(info = "<html><p>Lunar base subsystems.</p></html>")
  );
end LunarBase;

package.order lists the classes in display order:

Power
Thermal
Guidance

The compiler uses the package hierarchy for qualified lookup. It does not require a particular folder name to match a class name, but keeping them aligned makes the source tree readable and makes external tools happier.

docs.title: Qualified names and lookup
docs.text:
A class is identified by its qualified name:

within LunarBase.Power;

model Battery
  // ...
end Battery;

The full name is LunarBase.Power.Battery. An import shortens the spelling:

within LunarBase;

model Rover
  import Modelica.Blocks.Math;
  Math.Max maxBlock;
end Rover;

The compiler resolves the source's qualified roots and seats each known structured package before the DAE call. Every bundled source library follows the same admission contract. An unknown or unavailable root is a visible compile error rather than an implicit retry.

The editor uses the same root-segment rule. A cold qualified class requests its package root asynchronously; the canvas shows Loading and reprojects when the root is ready.

docs.title: What gets compiled
docs.text:
Compilation is closure-based, not folder-based. The compiler parses each unique URI once and installs the paired source and definition as one batch. The closure includes:

  • the selected class;
  • every class it references;
  • every package needed to resolve those names;
  • the admitted source roots.

A sibling .mo file that the selected class does not reference is not part of the closure. This is why two open documents can coexist without contaminating each other's compile source set.

Generated network sources consume their complete synthesized document and the admitted source roots, not other open Modelica documents. Their reserved generated/ filename namespace is classified by the runtime metadata owner and used for structural hashing.

docs.title: Browsing and inserting classes
docs.text:
The Package Browser is a Dymola-style tree of every admitted library and package. Clicking a class opens it in the Diagram and Code Editor, which share one ModelicaDocument; an edit in either view updates the other on the next frame.

The Component Palette is a search-first flat list of instantiable leaf components drawn from the same admitted roots. It filters by display name, full library path, category, and description. Dragging a row onto the Diagram instantiates it; insertion is disabled when no writable Modelica document is active.

A class that is present on disk but not admitted as a source root does not appear in either browser. Adding the root to [modelica].paths or [modelica].externals makes it visible after the Twin is reopened.

docs.title: Versioning and reproducibility
docs.text:
A library version is part of the build identity. The compiler's persistent artifact cache includes the library generation and the exact source content identity. A compiler upgrade or a changed library cannot admit an artifact from another build.

For reproducible projects:

  • pin downloaded library versions and hashes in the asset manifest or a Twin Assets.toml;
  • keep package.mo and package.order in version control;
  • avoid absolute external paths in a shared Twin;
  • record the library version in the Twin's README or manifest description;
  • re-run validation after a library upgrade.

A binary asset such as a downloaded library archive is content-hashed. A hash mismatch rejects the download rather than installing unverified bytes.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause Fix Class not found Source root not admitted Add the path to [modelica].paths or externals Package not found Missing package.mo or wrong within Fix the package structure or the within clause Duplicate class Two roots define the same qualified name Remove one root or rename the package Stale behavior after upgrade Cached artifact from another build Recompile; the cache key includes the library generation Library missing at startup Dataset not downloaded Open Settings → Data & libraries and install it

A missing library is not silently replaced by a built-in class. The compile fails with the qualified name it could not resolve.

docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Treat package.mo and package.order as part of the source, not as metadata.
  • Pin external libraries by version and hash.
  • Keep project packages under the Twin; keep shared libraries outside it.
  • Do not rely on an absolute path in a Twin you intend to share.
  • Recompile after changing a library; the closure may have changed.
  • Read the first compiler diagnostic; later errors are often consequences.

Continue with Experiments, which run a compiled model many times over swept parameters.

docs.title: Lunica
docs.text:
Lunica is the Modelica workbench. It runs as the ∿ Lunica perspective in the simulator and as the standalone lunica application. Both hosts embed the same compiler, execution, and workbench plugins, so a model behaves the same way in either one.

Lunica edits the same ModelicaDocument that the Twin uses, compiles through the same Rumoca session, and runs the same worker. The difference is presentation: Lunica adds the model browser, diagram, icon and documentation views, parameter inspector, and plots.

docs.title: The layout
docs.text:
Area Contents Twin browser Project files and the Modelica section with packages, classes, and libraries Component palette Insertable components, below the Twin browser Center Welcome page or open model tabs Model views Text, Diagram, Icon, Docs Model Inspector Parameters, real-time inputs, variables, and the selected component Graphs Live and completed-run trajectories Experiments Batch runs and parameter sweeps

The default Lunica perspective docks the Twin browser and component palette on the left, the model workspace in the center, and the Model Inspector on the right. Graphs, Experiments, Diagnostics, and Journal open from the View menu and default to the bottom dock.

A model opens in its own tab. Switching views does not remount the document; the text, diagram, icon, and docs views all read the same source.

docs.title: Opening and creating models
docs.text:
To open an existing model:

  1. Switch to ∿ Lunica.
  2. Open the Modelica section in the Twin browser.
  3. Expand a library or workspace document, then choose a class.

To create a model, use File → New → Modelica Model, the New Model button on the welcome page, or New Model in an empty Modelica workspace. Lunica creates an untitled in-memory document with the skeleton

model Untitled
end Untitled;

and opens it in a tab. There is no setup dialog. Rename the draft in the Twin browser by double-clicking its row, or edit the declaration in Text. For an untitled document the tab title follows the first top-level class name, and Save As proposes <class>.mo starting from the Twin root.

docs.title: Text view
docs.text:
The text view is a plain source editor over the authoritative .mo text. It supports word wrap, auto indent, and text scale in Settings → Modelica → Code Editor. The preferences persist under modelica_code_editor.

Editing text produces a typed ModelicaOp. The document reparses at a defined boundary, and the diagram, inspector, and compiler see the same change. There is no second source buffer.

docs.title: Diagram view
docs.text:
The diagram is a thin view over the document. It renders authored Modelica icons, routed connections, and editable placements on the workbench canvas. Dragging a component or a connection produces an operation; it does not write text directly.

Action Result Drag from the palette Add a component Drag a component Change its placement Drag between ports Add a connect equation Select a component Inspect its parameters Double-click a component Drill into its class Scroll Zoom the canvas; with semantic zoom enabled, reveal nested diagrams

The add-component menu hides partial classes by default. Settings → Modelica → Show partial classes includes them. A class without authored placement uses a deterministic grid; a class without an icon uses the renderer's named component presentation. These are presentation defaults.

Semantic zoom is opt-in. Enable Modelica semantic zoom in Settings → Appearance to scroll into a component and reveal its nested diagram and source equations; double-click still opens the component for editing.

A conditional declaration is marked as conditional, including a literal if true. The compiler owns condition evaluation and compiled instance presence; the diagram does not infer active instances from a Boolean expression.

docs.title: Icon and docs views
docs.text:
The Icon view edits the class's Icon annotation. The Docs view renders the class's Documentation annotation and the selected documentation fragments.

Both are views over authored source. An edit in the icon view changes the Icon annotation in the model text.

docs.title: Compile
docs.text:
Compile builds the selected class through Rumoca. A successful compile leaves the model ready and paused. A failed compile reports the phase diagnostic with its source location; the previous artifact is not used as a silent fallback.

The compiler admits each unique URI once and installs the paired source and definition as one batch. Single-source and multi-source compilation share that boundary. A changed owned source, mixed ownership, or conflicting contents under one URI fails before overlay installation.

Compilation is asynchronous. A heartbeat reports progress, and the worker catches panics and reports them as solver errors rather than crashing the application. This tolerance is essential for interactive parameter tuning: an unstable parameter should not kill the whole simulation.

docs.title: Run and Fast Run
docs.text:
Action Clock Use Run Wall-clock simulation Inspect a live model, tune parameters, watch plots Fast Run Batch, as fast as possible Parameter studies, regression checks, comparisons

Run starts a live session. The model advances with the simulation clock and can be paused, resumed, or reset. Fast Run executes from t_start to t_end through the experiment runner and produces a trajectory.

Fast Run uses the model's experiment annotation for default bounds. Invalid annotation bounds return an error through the same resolver; they do not select the default. The shared bounds guard rejects invalid explicit inputs and grids beyond the sample cap before solver allocation.

A live solver step failure keeps the solver error and lists the values that were not produced by the failed step, with their last accepted samples.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
The Model Inspector edits live parameters through SetModelicaParameter. The command edits the declaration in the participant's selected class, leaves the document dirty, and reinitializes the participant with the checked replacement. Saving the document makes the new value the type default; other instance overrides remain intact.

USD-backed controls require editing their authored USD binding and are disabled in the document-only inspector path. A value that belongs to one scene instance belongs in USD; a value that belongs to the type belongs in the .mo file.

docs.title: Inspector and plots
docs.text:
The Model Inspector lists parameters, real-time inputs, and variables. Ticking a variable routes its samples to the active plot, or to the plot chosen in Plot in. The Graphs panel renders live and completed-run trajectories through the shared visualization layer.

History is retained by the Modelica telemetry plane using the shared recording rate, channel limit, and retention settings. The same retention plane is installed for standalone Modelica hosts and the full mission sampler.

docs.title: Document identity
docs.text:
A Modelica document has three identity views:

Tier Source of truth Used by File Document origin (untitled or file path) Save, dirty check, file browser Workspace entry DocumentEntry.title, derived from the first top-level class Recents and workspace lists Modelica class AST top-level class name Compile, references, class browser, journal

The class name is authoritative for compilation and references, as in Dymola and OMEdit. For an untitled draft the origin name follows the first top-level class, so the tab title does too. A saved file keeps its file stem as the tab title; a drilled-in tab shows the class short name.

Renaming a class rewrites the declaration and its end OLD; closer. Renaming an untitled draft in the Twin browser also updates the draft origin, so the tab title follows. Renaming a saved .mo file in the Twin browser updates the open document's top-level class to the new stem and saves it, keeping the Foo.mo / model Foo convention when the class still matches the old stem. Renaming the class inside the editor does not rename the file.

docs.title: A practical workflow
docs.text:
1. Open or create the model.
  2. Work in Diagram for structure and Text for equations.
  3. Compile and fix diagnostics before attaching the model to a scene.
  4. Run live to inspect behavior and tune parameters.
  5. Use Fast Run to compare variants or check a bound.
  6. Save the document, then attach it to a USD prim through LunCoProgramAPI.
  7. Run the scene and inspect the authored ports in Analyze.

The model is ready to attach when it compiles cleanly and its public outputs are declared. A model that only runs in Lunica but has no declared outputs cannot drive anything in the scene.

docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Treat the class as the identity; the file is an implementation detail.
  • Compile before attaching. The scene runs the compiled artifact.
  • Keep type defaults in the .mo file and instance overrides in USD.
  • Use Fast Run for comparisons and Run live for inspection.
  • Fix the source diagnostic; do not tune around a failed compile.
  • Save before closing a tab with a dirty marker.

Continue with Libraries, which explains where packages and the standard library come from.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The reference chapters describe exact surfaces: command-line flags, file formats, manifest fields, API envelopes, validation gates, and known failure modes. They are written to be consulted, not read end to end.

Use the tutorials for a guided flow and the domain chapters for concepts. Use this chapter when you need the exact spelling of a flag, the owner of a file, or the evidence required before making a claim.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: Section Use it for Command line Startup flags, recording, networking, Rhai REPL, scene tests, asset validation Controls Shipped keyboard, mouse, camera, and workbench bindings twin.toml Project identity, entry scene, source roots, settings, children, journal Assets.toml External downloads, hashes, processing recipes, cache behavior File formats Extensions, JSON kinds, generated files, and runtime state HTTP API Request envelope, endpoints, schema discovery, readiness Mission control Operator lifecycle, authority claims, telemetry, release Validation Preflight, lint, scene tests, SysML verification, evidence Troubleshooting Startup, scene, input, asset, Modelica, telemetry, and API failures

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Paths. A path in a manifest is relative to that manifest's owner unless the text says otherwise. twin.toml paths are Twin-relative. Assets.toml destinations are Twin-relative or cache-relative. Runtime UI manifest paths are relative to the scope's asset root and are qualified with lunco:// or twin:// before publication.

Commands. Command names are exact and case-sensitive. Discover them from the running build with GET /api/commands/schema; do not infer a name from a menu label. A rejected command is terminal and does not partially apply.

Values. A missing value is not zero. A port can be absent while its owner is preparing. An omitted setting inherits; an explicit false is a value.

Evidence. A parse check is not a runtime test. A screenshot is not numerical evidence. A passing test must come from a real verdict, not from the absence of a failure.

docs.title: Source of truth
docs.text:
When this documentation and the running build disagree, the build wins:

  1. The reflected command and query schema of the running binary.
  2. The authored asset or manifest actually loaded by that build.
  3. The current source in the engine repository.
  4. This documentation.

That order is deliberate. The schema is generated from the registered types, and a manifest is validated before it is mounted. Prose can lag a rename; the running surface cannot.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• How it fits together — the runtime flow behind these surfaces
  • Formats — which authored format owns which fact
  • Glossary — terms used across the reference
  • Integrate your stack — supported boundaries and adapter responsibilities

docs.title: Assets.toml
docs.text:
Assets.toml declares external bytes that a Twin or the engine needs but does not store in the project: source libraries, terrain rasters, textures, fonts, and downloadable models.

It is a manifest, not a scene file and not a cache. The actual files are downloaded to a local cache and addressed from USD or Modelica through logical asset URIs.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
• A Twin can have an Assets.toml at its root. Destinations resolve against the Twin.
  • The engine ships manifests under assets/manifests/*.toml using the same entry format. Each file is a group such as modelica, fonts, terrain, or celestial.

docs.title: A basic entry
docs.text:
[modelica_standard_library]
name = "Modelica Standard Library"
version = "4.1.0"
url = "https://github.com/modelica/ModelicaStandardLibrary/archive/refs/tags/v4.1.0.tar.gz"
dest = "library"
sha256 = "<sha256 of the archive>"

A single-file dataset uses the same shape:

[site_dem]
name = "Site terrain DEM"
url = "https://example.org/site-dem.tif"
dest = "assets/terrain/site-dem.tif"
sha256 = "<sha256 of the file>"

The table key is the asset key. It is what --asset / -a uses on the assets manager CLI.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Meaning name Human-readable name used in progress and diagnostics url Download source dest Destination relative to the Twin root or engine cache version Version marker checked when validating an installed archive sha256 Expected content hash; the download is rejected on mismatch extract Archive-internal path to extract into dest shared Put the download in the shared global cache instead of the Twin-local cache recommended Offer the dataset during onboarding when it is missing process Optional processing recipe for a downloaded source bundle Binary names whose package should contain this artifact package_only Build-time package input, excluded from the runtime download catalog

dest is a portable relative path. Absolute paths, parent traversal, and platform-specific path syntax are rejected.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
A download can be followed by a processing step. A compound recipe uses kind = "pipeline" and must declare both the final artifacts and the ordered steps that produce them:

[site_dem.process]
kind = "pipeline"
output_root = "cache"
output = "terrain/site"
center_lat = -85.0
center_lon = 30.0
window_m = 1024.0
target_resolution = [257, 257]
frame = "MOON_ME"

[site_dem.process.pipeline]
artifacts = [
  { from = "height",
    source = "materials/textures/heightmap.tif",
    path = "materials/textures/heightmap.tif",
    kind = "dem",
    dimensions = [257, 257] },
]

[[site_dem.process.pipeline.steps]]
id = "height"
input = "source"
kind = "dem"
output = "height"

The artifacts table is the final consumer contract; a planner cannot replace it. A step input names source, another declared input, or an earlier step. Scratch outputs must be distinct and may not overlap.

Processing is optional. If the downloaded bytes are already the artifact you need, omit process.

docs.title: Runtime behavior
docs.text:
LunCoSim does not download in the background on launch. A missing declared dataset is shown to the user, and the download starts only after an explicit request. The same declarations are visible in Settings → Data & libraries and in the Twin's assets view.

The shared cache is:

Platform Default cache Linux ~/.cache/lunco/ macOS ~/Library/Caches/lunco/ Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\lunco\

Set LUNCOSIM_CACHE to override the cache root. Twin-scoped declarations write beside the Twin by default unless the entry is marked shared = true.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The assets manager in the source checkout can inspect and fetch a Twin's manifest:

cargo run -p lunco-assets -- list -t path/to/twin
cargo run -p lunco-assets -- download -t path/to/twin
cargo run -p lunco-assets -- process -t path/to/twin

Use -a <key> to target one entry, --force to replace an installed artifact, and --quality coarse|good to choose a faster or full processing bake.

docs.title: Addressing the result
docs.text:
Authored files never address the physical cache path. Use:

  • lunco://... for the installed engine asset library
  • twin://... for a file inside the open Twin

The asset registry resolves the logical URI to the installed bytes. A USD layer that hardcodes ~/.cache/lunco/... is not portable and does not use this contract.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• USD — how assets are referenced from a scene
  • Twin — the project that can declare its own assets
  • Troubleshooting — missing or failed downloads

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The luncosim binary can open the desktop app, serve the API headlessly, run a scene test, validate assets, or connect the Rhai REPL to a running session.

luncosim [FLAGS]
luncosim rhai [--api PORT] [-e SNIPPET | -f FILE]
luncosim test --scene PATH
luncosim --validate PATH…

Run luncosim --help for the help text of the installed version.

docs.title: Startup
docs.text:
Flag Meaning --scene PATH Load this USD scene at startup. The path may be relative to assets/, to the current directory, or absolute --api [PORT] Serve the HTTP command API on the given port --no-ui Run headless, without a window. Also LUNCO_NO_UI=1 --window-pos SPEC Place the window: left, right, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right. X11/XWayland only; native Wayland ignores it --validate PATH… Parse-check asset files and exit without opening a window or GPU

--no-ui does not imply --api. Pass both when a headless run needs the API:

luncosim --no-ui --api 4101 --scene scenes/tests/rover.usda

Without --scene, the app starts with an empty persistent world shell. The sandbox is an explicit scene or lesson, not an implicit startup default.

docs.title: Recording and capture
docs.text:
Flag Meaning --record-offline <dir|out.mp4> Record deterministic frames. A directory receives a PNG sequence; a video path streams to ffmpeg --record-fps N Output frame rate; default 60 --record-preset MODE H.264 preset; default ultrafast --record-frames N Stop after N frames --offscreen Render windowlessly into an offscreen target and exit when the take drains --record-size WxH Offscreen target resolution; default 1280x720

A one-command windowless take:

luncosim --offscreen --scene scenes/demo.usda \
  --record-offline /tmp/demo.mp4 --record-frames 300

Recording is deterministic once the scene is ready. Do not judge render cost from a recording run; use a separate profiling session.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
Flag Meaning --host [PORT] Host a WebTransport session; default port 5888 --connect ADDR Join a hosted session; a missing port implies port 5888 --cert PATH TLS certificate: a certbot live directory or a certificate file --key PATH TLS private key when --cert names a file

Omit --cert and --key for a development self-signed certificate. A bare IP address for --connect skips TLS validation for a LAN/development run.

Networking is opt-in at build time. A default local build does not start a multiplayer host.

docs.title: Rendering and performance
docs.text:
Flag Meaning --render-profile MODE standard preserves authored PBR; fast uses unlit, texture-free materials and disables HDR, bloom, and MSAA --render-quality MODE low, balanced, or high graphics budgets --no-vsync Uncap the frame rate --no-throttle Keep running at full rate while unfocused --headless-max-speed With --no-ui, advance the fixed simulation lattice as fast as the CPU and causal participants allow --log-diag Log FPS, frame-time, and physics diagnostics --console Windows: enable the debug console for this launch

--render-quality changes GPU budgets; it does not replace the shaders authored by the scene. When measuring FPS, use --no-vsync --no-throttle so you are not timing the compositor or the unfocused power-save throttle.

docs.title: Rhai REPL
docs.text:
Connect to a running instance's API port:

luncosim rhai --api 4101
luncosim rhai --api 4101 -e 'print(find("Rover"))'
luncosim rhai --api 4101 -f scripts/check.rhai

The REPL evaluates against the live app. It is useful for inspection and small commands; authored tests belong in a scene test.

docs.title: Scene tests
docs.text:
luncosim test --scene assets/scenes/tests/rover_drive.usda
luncosim test --list

A scene test runs the authored Rhai test headlessly and deterministically. The exit code is the verdict:

Exit Meaning 0 PASS 1 FAIL 2 No verdict was produced Option Meaning --list List discovered test scenes and their execution kind --verdict-channel NAME Accept the verdict only from this channel --verification QUALIFIED_NAME Require a Twin manifest SysML verification mapping --max-ticks N Bound cumulative fixed steps; default 20000 --tick-hz HZ Manual update rate; default 60 --readiness-timeout SECS Bound scene and participant preparation; default 420 --determinism-reference PATH Load a typed JSON state reference for Rhai comparisons --threads N Compute-pool width; 1 is the gate profile --jitter FRAC / --seed U64 Exercise seeded fractional-dt pacing

A component-level suite selects its own scene from the Twin manifest:

luncosim test-component --twin path/to/twin --component rover.wheels

Run the production binary for these checks; do not substitute a private test harness or --validate. --validate only proves that the files parse and their declarations are structurally valid. See Validation for the evidence layers.

docs.title: Asset validation
docs.text:
luncosim --validate path/to/model.mo path/to/scene.usda

Supported inputs include .mo, .usda, .sysml, .kerml, .wesl, and .rhai. The command is parse-only: no window, GPU, or app launch. It exits 0 when every input is valid and 1 when any input fails.

docs.text:

  • Install — packaged and source builds

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: These are the shipped default bindings. Tutorials and lessons show the current binding through input_hint(...), so rebinding an action updates both the control and the on-screen hint.

docs.title: Movement
docs.text:
Action Default Forward W Backward S Left A Right D Yaw left Q Yaw right E Speed boost Shift

The same movement set applies to walking and to driving. A vehicle first needs to be possessed; selection alone does not send input to it.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action Default Context action F Thrust / brake Space Release G Switch mode V Pause P Cancel Backspace or Escape Delete selection Delete

Space is both thrust and brake depending on the controlled vehicle and mode. The active control mode decides which effect applies.

docs.title: Camera and selection
docs.text:
Action Default Look / orbit Hold right mouse button and move Select Left click Extend selection Shift + left click Remove from selection Ctrl + left click Drill into an assembly Alt + Shift + left click Add route point Alt + left click Route context menu Right click

Middle-button look is available when configured. The default look button is the right mouse button.

docs.title: Workbench shortcuts
docs.text: Action Default Find navigation target Ctrl + P Find action Ctrl + Shift + P Navigate back Alt + ← Navigate forward Alt + → Save document Ctrl + S Save as Ctrl + Shift + S Close document Ctrl + W New document Ctrl + N Open file Ctrl + O Compile F5 Undo Ctrl + Z Redo Ctrl + Shift + Z or Ctrl + Y

docs.title: Rebinding
docs.text:
Open Settings → Keybindings and change the action, not the physical key in a tutorial. The authored defaults are the input-bindings document discovered by kind lunco.input-bindings.v1; in a source checkout that document is assets/config/keybindings.json. Your edits persist in the input_bindings section of settings.json, not in the authored asset.

A lesson that uses input_hint("forward") displays the effective binding. A lesson that hardcodes a key name is not using the controller-owned binding contract.

A Twin can displace a conflicting lower-priority physical binding while it is active. The displaced action and the winning action are reported in Recent Events; your global preference stays stored and returns when the Twin closes.

docs.title: Gamepad and alternate input
docs.text: The input layer maps semantic intents, so an alternate device or a remapped keyboard supplies the same actions. The UI and lessons consume the intent, not the raw key. If an added device does not respond, check that it is mapped to the same intent in the input settings.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text:
A LunCoSim project is a set of authored sources plus a small amount of runtime state. The authored sources keep their native formats. LunCoSim extensions are carried in standard USD, Modelica, Rhai, TOML, JSON, and WESL constructs rather than in a private project archive.

This page is the extension-and-owner index. For the conceptual division between USD, Modelica, Rhai, and TOML, see Formats.

docs.title: Authored domain files
docs.text:
Extension Format Owns Consumer .usd, .usda, .usdc USD stage Hierarchy, transforms, geometry, materials, physics, typed ports, connections, program attachments USD composition, renderer, physics, co-simulation .usdz Packaged USD A self-contained USD package, when the registered USD file-format plugin is available USD composition .gltf, .glb glTF 2.0 asset Mesh geometry, materials, node hierarchy Bevy glTF loader through the USD render adapter .mo Modelica source Continuous equations, parameters, state, acausal connectors Modelica compiler and solver .fmu FMI 3 Co-Simulation archive An external co-simulation participant Native FMI 3 CS importer; scalar Float64 profile .rhai Rhai script Events, commands, tasks, objectives, tutorial flow, test verdicts Rhai runtime and tool hooks .wesl WESL shader source Parameter block, texture bindings, fragment and optional vertex entry points Shader reflection and render pipeline .sysml, .kerml SysML/KerML source Requirements, structure, verification mappings Bounded SysML validation and Rhai analysis twin.toml TOML Project identity, entry scene, source roots, settings, children, journal policy Workspace and Twin loader Assets.toml TOML External bytes, hashes, processing recipes, cache placement Asset registry and downloader

The native FMI importer is deliberately narrow. It supports scalar Float64 signals and rejects Event Mode, early return, Model Exchange, arrays, Scheduled Execution clocks, and externally hosted FMUs. A .fmu that loads is not a claim of broad FMI conformance; state the tested profile when reporting a result.

glTF is an external asset format, not a USD layer. A USD payload or reference arc names the file, and the render adapter reads that arc from the composed prim and loads the asset through Bevy's glTF loader. The default lunco:assetMode = "scene" attaches the whole scene; "mesh" attaches one mesh primitive as Mesh3d. lunco:assetLabel selects a named sub-asset. The same asset path works in native and browser builds. See Addresses and assets.

docs.title: Engine and policy manifests
docs.text:
These files are authored data, even when they ship with the engine:

Path Kind or format Purpose assets/manifests/*.toml TOML Grouped engine asset declarations for Modelica, fonts, terrain, celestial data, and environment data assets/scripting/policy/index.toml TOML with kind = "lunco.policy.v1" Binds hook ids to Rhai sources and entry points assets/config/keybindings.json JSON with kind = "lunco.input-bindings.v1" Authored default input bindings assets/config/program_contracts.json JSON with kind = "lunco.program-contracts.v1" Program contract declarations assets/ui/runtime_surfaces.json JSON with kind = "lunco.runtime-ui-manifest.v1" Shipped runtime UI surfaces

A Twin can carry its own Assets.toml, policy manifest, input bindings, program contracts, and runtime UI manifest. The engine discovers authored documents by kind, not by a compiled-in filename.

docs.title: Runtime UI documents
docs.text:
A runtime UI manifest names its templates and stylesheets:

Extension Role .json lunco.runtime-ui-manifest.v1 surface registration .html HUI template: retained tree, declared properties, callbacks .css Flair stylesheet: appearance, internal layout, custom properties .ttf Bundled font asset referenced by runtime_fonts.css

Paths in a manifest are relative to that scope's asset root. The runtime qualifies them with lunco:// or twin:// before publishing the retained tree. See Runtime UI.

docs.title: User and workspace state
docs.text:
These files are written by the application, not authored by hand:

Path Content <OS config dir>/lunco/settings.json User-global typed settings sections <OS config dir>/lunco/settings.json.bad Preserved copy of an unreadable settings file <OS config dir>/lunco/recents.json Bounded recent Twin and file lists <OS config dir>/lunco/workspace-state/<fnv1a-hex>.json Per-Twin workspace state: active perspective, open documents, dock layout, draggable runtime-window overrides <project>/.lunco/settings.json Project-local settings override <twin>/history/journal.json Edit journal, when [journal].persist = true

LUNCOSIM_CONFIG replaces the user configuration directory. LUNCOSIM_CACHE replaces the asset cache root. Do not hardcode either path in a USD layer; use lunco:// or twin://.

A project-local .lunco/settings.json is excluded from Twin distribution. A workspace-state file is keyed by a hash of the project path and is not written into the Twin folder. That keeps personal layout state out of a shared project.

docs.title: Evidence and capture outputs
docs.text:
Output Produced by Use .png sequence --record-offline <dir> Deterministic frame capture .mp4 --record-offline <file>.mp4 Video capture through ffmpeg .png CaptureScreenshot Visual evidence from the visible production window .lcsin ExportSessionInputCapture Bounded session input archive on a native host JSON state reference Authored test fixture Determinism comparison for Rhai tests

An .lcsin archive is an input record, not a complete replay package. It does not contain a baseline manifest or a playback consumer, and not every command is in the input slice. Do not claim bit-reproducible mission replay from it.

docs.title: JSON kind discriminators
docs.text:
A JSON document that participates in a registry declares its contract in a kind field. The important user-facing kinds are:

Kind Document lunco.runtime-ui-manifest.v1 Runtime UI surface manifest lunco.input-bindings.v1 Authored input bindings lunco.program-contracts.v1 Program contract catalog lunco.tutorial-catalog.v1 Tutorial catalog lunco.policy.v1 Policy manifest (TOML) lunco.lunar-surface-continuation.v1 Lunar surface continuation recipe lunco.surface-annotations.v1 Surface annotation data lunco.volume-depth.v1 Volume depth data lunco.shadow-receiver.surface.v1 Shadow-receiver surface data

A document with the wrong kind is not silently accepted by another registry. Unknown fields are rejected by the manifest loaders that use strict schemas.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Keep the native format valid. A .mo file should still open in another Modelica tool, and a .usda file should still open in another USD application.
  • Reference glTF through a USD payload or reference. It is an external asset, not a composable USD layer.
  • Do not edit a generated or cached artifact by hand. Author the source and let the pipeline produce the result.
  • Do not hardcode a cache path in a scene. Use lunco:// or twin://.
  • Do not put equations in USD, mission policy in Modelica, or physics integration in Rhai.
  • Do not add a Rust special case for one rover, lesson, or asset. Use the authored contract.
