docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• A movable mounted part needs a body and a joint.
  • Author mass explicitly when the collider volume is not the real mass.
  • Keep joint axes and anchors in the joint's local frames; do not compensate with body transforms.
  • Filter the pairs you mean. Joint adjacency is the only automatic case.
  • Use PhysicsCollisionGroup when pair relationships stop scaling.
  • Keep semantic sensor logic in Modelica; keep the raw ray in USD.
  • Expect unsupported schemas to be rejected or reported, never silently approximated.

Continue with Ports and connections, where physical bodies and programs exchange typed values.

docs.title: Ports and connections
docs.text: A scene becomes a system when its parts exchange values. LunCoSim expresses that exchange as typed USD properties and standard USD connections. The same authored wire feeds co-simulation, telemetry, the Ports panel, and the HTTP API; there is no second signal graph.

docs.title: The three property namespaces
docs.text:
Namespace Direction Meaning inputs:<name> Into the prim A value the component consumes outputs:<name> Out of the prim A value the component publishes connectors:<name> Acausal A Modelica connector exposed on the component boundary

A scalar port is a typed USD attribute. The type is part of the contract:

def Xform "Rover" (kind = "assembly")
{
    float inputs:throttle = 0.0
    float inputs:steer = 0.0
    float outputs:speed = 0.0
    double outputs:odometer = 0.0
}

inputs: and outputs: are causal: the producer writes, the consumer reads. connectors: describe an acausal Modelica interface, where the equation system decides the direction. A connector property without a connection is reported as an orphan warning; it is not silently treated as a causal port.

docs.title: Authoring a connection
docs.text:
A connection is authored on the property that consumes the value:

def Xform "DescentLander" (
    prepend apiSchemas = ["PhysicsRigidBodyAPI", "LunCoProgramAPI"]
)
{
    uniform token info:implementationSource = "sourceAsset"
    uniform asset info:sourceAsset = @lunco://models/Lander.mo@
    uniform bool lunco:program:realtimeSafe = true

    float inputs:external_throttle = 0.0
    float outputs:throttle

    def Scope "MainPropulsion"
    {
        float inputs:valve_opening.connect = </DescentLander.outputs:throttle>
    }
}

The target path is the source. In the composed stage the connection resolves to a SimConnection with a source prim and property, a sink prim and property, and a scalar type. The runtime compiles that graph into dense target indices and propagates values at the fixed step.

A connection is not a value copy. It is a topology fact that survives recomposition. If the source is renamed or removed, the wire is reported as invalid rather than silently reading zero.

docs.title: The public-output rule
docs.text:
A model output becomes externally connectable only when the component prim declares the matching outputs:<name> property. A path mentioned only as a connection target does not create a public port.

This rule prevents a connection from reaching into a model's private state. The model may compute hundreds of local variables; only the declared outputs are part of its interface.

def Xform "ReactionWheel" (
    prepend apiSchemas = ["LunCoProgramAPI"]
)
{
    uniform token info:implementationSource = "sourceAsset"
    uniform asset info:sourceAsset = @twin://rover/models/ReactionWheel.mo@

    # Public interface: these are the only values another prim may consume.
    float outputs:torque = 0.0
    float outputs:speed = 0.0
}

The matching Modelica class must declare the same names as outputs. A declaration mismatch is a compile-time interface error, not a runtime surprise.

docs.title: Types, units, and bounds
docs.text:
The scalar port surface is f64 at the runtime boundary. USD may author a narrower type (float, double, int, bool), and the adapter preserves the authored type for validation and display. A write that would narrow a value at the GPU or command boundary is checked there; the port registry itself keeps the exact sample.

Port metadata carries:

Field Purpose type Authored scalar type unit Engineering unit, when known bounds Valid range, when authored or supplied by the owner source Backend label such as Modelica, Avian, or a script authority Which owner may write the port writable Whether a command may write it

Compatible unit conversions are compiled into the connection fabric. An incompatible unit is a wiring error, not an invitation to guess a factor.

docs.title: Direction and ownership
docs.text:
Every port has exactly one declared owner. The PortRegistry selects that owner from the composed declarations and the live backend state. A source wire retains the authored prim and port identity; wiring does not redirect a source around the owner's decision.

A value that is both authored as an output and written by an imperative producer is a conflict. OutputPorts stores values for an imperative producer; it is not a second signal graph and must not shadow a solver-owned output.

For a Modelica participant:

  • Checked DAE runtime inputs define writable ports.
  • Numeric observables, including authored outputs and local states, define readable values that USD may export.
  • Constants, runtime inputs, and parameters are not published as participant output samples.
  • Reading a local state does not make it writable.

docs.title: Initial admission
docs.text:
At t = 0, source interfaces and native physical definitions become available before numerical admission. Acyclic participants initialize from finite producer samples. Participants with complete initial inputs enter independent preparation without delaying a separate coupled plan.

Required external outputs still wait for their registered initial expressions or samples. Absent values remain pending rather than defaulting to zero.

When the remaining participants depend on one another, the owner captures their exact source, authored bindings, scene generation, and ordered wiring. The synth.coupled-initialization hook emits a Modelica composite containing those instances, their input bindings, and input probes. The composite is compiled and initialized as a request-owned job; its finite observations must agree with the connected graph within solver tolerance before the members are released together.

A changed source or wire cannot release an old certificate. Failed certification reports a terminal runtime fault and holds the affected participants.

docs.title: Reading the graph
docs.text:
QueryUsdPrim exposes the composed port surface. ReadPorts exposes live values with owner-supplied metadata. ListPorts enumerates the declared names for an entity.

The CausalTrace query joins one semantic edge to its authored binding, selected port owner, USD/Avian admission state, current measured channels, producer origin, and optional fixed-tick admission stamp:

let edge = intent_pulse(target, "release");
let trace = query("CausalTrace", #{
    target: target,
    correlation_id: edge.id,
});

An absent or pending stage is an incomplete path, not successful actuation. Omitting correlation_id selects the newest trace for the target.

docs.title: Authoring through the document
docs.text:
The Editor and scripts do not rewrite USDA text to add a wire. They use the typed SetConnection operation:

SetConnection {
    edit_target,
    path: "/Rover",
    name: "inputs:throttle",
    type_name: "float",
    sources: ["/Driver.outputs:throttle"],
}

SetConnection is journaled with its inverse and replayed onto the live stage. The typed connection preflight resolves referenced providers and applied API schemas through the edited document's own authoring recipe. Runtime-only endpoints are checked against the live port registry, so another open Twin cannot change whether an authored wire is valid.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
A drive-by-wire rover has a Modelica controller, a physics chassis, and a Rhai mission:

def Xform "Rover" (kind = "assembly")
{
    def Scope "Controller" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["LunCoProgramAPI"]
    )
    {
        uniform token info:implementationSource = "sourceAsset"
        uniform asset info:sourceAsset = @twin://rover/models/Drive.mo@
        uniform bool lunco:program:realtimeSafe = true

        float inputs:throttle = 0.0
        float inputs:steer = 0.0
        float outputs:left_torque = 0.0
        float outputs:right_torque = 0.0
    }

    def Xform "Chassis" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["PhysicsRigidBodyAPI"]
    )
    {
        float inputs:left_torque.connect = </Rover/Controller.outputs:left_torque>
        float inputs:right_torque.connect = </Rover/Controller.outputs:right_torque>
    }
}

The mission script writes throttle and steer through SetPorts. The controller reads them, computes wheel torques, and publishes the two outputs. The chassis consumes the torques. The same values are visible in the Ports panel and over the API without a second publication path.

docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Declare every consumed value as an outputs: property on the producer.
  • Author the wire on the consumer, pointing at the producer.
  • Keep one owner per port. Do not shadow a solver output with an imperative write.
  • Use connectors: only for genuine acausal Modelica interfaces.
  • Expect missing initial samples to hold admission; do not substitute zero.
  • Inspect a disputed value with CausalTrace before adding another wire.
  • Add connections through SetConnection, never by editing text behind the document's back.

Continue with Programs, which attach the behavior that reads and writes these ports.

docs.title: Programs
docs.text:
A program is the behavior attached to a prim. Modelica, Rhai, and optionally Python programs all use the same LunCoProgramAPI schema and the same source-backed lifecycle. The schema applies directly to the physical prim when the behavior is intrinsic, or to a child Scope when the behavior is separable.

This is a deliberate simplification. There is no global script list, no scene-level controller registry, and no hidden behavior that survives deleting the program prim or the object that owns it.

docs.title: The program prim
docs.text:
def Xform "Rover" (kind = "assembly")
{
    def Scope "Controller" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["LunCoProgramAPI"]
    )
    {
        uniform token info:implementationSource = "sourceAsset"
        uniform asset info:sourceAsset = @twin://my-rover/models/Drive.mo@
        uniform bool lunco:program:realtimeSafe = true
    }
}
Property Meaning info:implementationSource "sourceAsset" for a file, "sourceCode" for inline text, "id" for a runtime-implemented driver info:sourceAsset Asset address of the source file info:sourceCode Inline source text, when using sourceCode lunco:program:realtimeSafe Declares that the program can meet the real-time step budget

The example uses a child Scope, the separable placement: the controller is bolted onto the rover and can be removed without removing the airframe. Apply the same schema directly to the physical prim when the program is the thing itself — a lander's flight-control system, for example — so its inputs: are the vehicle's control surface. In both placements the ports live on the prim that carries the schema, and a connection targets those ports.

For a source asset, the backend is selected from its extension:

Extension Backend .mo Modelica .rhai Rhai .py Python, when the optional feature is built

A missing or unrecognized extension is an explicit program error. It is not guessed from the prim name or the folder.

docs.title: Implementation arms
docs.text:
Use sourceAsset for anything a person will edit, review, or reuse:

uniform token info:implementationSource = "sourceAsset"
uniform asset info:sourceAsset = @lunco://models/RoverDrive.mo@

Use sourceCode only for small, generated, or test-only programs:

uniform token info:implementationSource = "sourceCode"
uniform string info:sourceCode = "fn on_start(me, ctx) { notify(\"ready\"); }"

Use id for a driver the runtime already implements, such as range_beam. The selected arm is authoritative: exactly one of info:id, info:sourceAsset, or info:sourceCode may be populated. A populated non-selected arm is an authoring conflict, not a fallback.

A file-backed program participates in the asset pipeline: it reloads when the file changes, resolves its imports through the asset owner, and can be opened in the appropriate editor. Inline source has none of that provenance. It is appropriate for a fixture, not for a project a team maintains.

docs.title: Attaching a program
docs.text:
The typed authoring intent is AttachProgram. It authors the child prim, declared scalar ports, defaults, and USD connections as one change set. The same operation is exposed to scripts as assembly_edit::attach_program and to the UI as the program attachment flow.

Attaching a program is an ordinary USD edit. It enters the journal, can be undone, and is saved with the document. The runtime does not create a program prim behind the author's back.

AttachProgram attaches a child program to any prim that can own one. The common choices are the assembly root, a controller scope, or a dedicated behavior prim. Keep the program near the thing it controls so deleting the assembly deletes the behavior. For an intrinsic program, apply LunCoProgramAPI to the physical prim directly; that is a schema application rather than the child-prim flow.

docs.title: The realtime promise
docs.text:
lunco:program:realtimeSafe = true is a declaration, never an inference. No amount of reading a model's source establishes how long it takes to step.

The promise matters when a program writes a force or torque port on a client-predicted body. Without it, the wiring pass refuses that wire and reports the reason. This prevents a slow solver from being admitted into a path that must meet the presentation clock.

Absent or false means "not promised." A malformed value is ignored with a warning; it does not become true.

docs.title: Program lifecycle
docs.text:
A source-backed program follows the same sequence in every backend:

  1. The program prim is discovered during projection. For a child program, the owning prim is projected first.
  2. The source asset is resolved through the asset owner.
  3. The source is compiled or parsed into an interface.
  4. Declared ports and authored defaults are checked against that interface.
  5. Connected inputs are admitted, possibly through coupled initialization.
  6. The program starts and participates in the fixed-step clock.
  7. On detach, hot reload, or scene teardown, the old program stops before a replacement starts.

A terminal interface error faults the participant instead of leaving an unresolved readiness wait. Source replacement refreshes the same checked interface through its owner.

docs.title: Hot reload
docs.text:
Editing a file-backed program can reload it without rebuilding Rust. The outgoing program's stop hook runs before the new one starts. For Rhai this is on_stop; for Modelica it is session retirement and recompilation.

Hot reload is not a scene restart. The document, the stage, and unrelated participants stay live. A program that acquired control must release it in its stop hook.

docs.title: Modelica programs
docs.text:
A .mo program is a Modelica class compiled by Rumoca and run on a background worker. Its public ports come from the checked DAE, not from the source text alone:

  • runtime inputs are writable;
  • numeric observables, including authored outputs and local states, are readable;
  • constants, runtime inputs, and parameters are not published as outputs.

The program prim's inputs: and outputs: properties are the external contract. They must match the compiled interface. See Modelica for the language and Cosimulation for the step contract.

docs.title: Rhai programs
docs.text:
A .rhai program is a scenario with lifecycle hooks. It observes the simulation, reacts to events, and issues typed commands. It does not integrate physics or replace a Modelica model.

def Scope "Mission" (
    prepend apiSchemas = ["LunCoProgramAPI"]
) {
    uniform token info:implementationSource = "sourceAsset"
    uniform asset info:sourceAsset = @twin://my-rover/scenarios/drive.rhai@
}

The asset source is loaded and hot-replaced by the asset layer. A scenario can also be run directly against an entity with RunScenario, or run as a file-backed asset with RunScenarioAsset. See Rhai.

docs.title: Python programs
docs.text: Python is an optional feature. When built, a .py program is loaded through the same source-backed path. Python does not implement the scenario lifecycle hooks; it supports the one-shot RunPython command and a participant source seam. A build without the feature cannot execute or register Python participants.

docs.title: Several programs on one prim
docs.text:
A prim may own several program children, and it may also carry one intrinsic program of its own. Each program prim is an independent participant with its own source, session, and lifecycle. They interact through the same typed ports and event bus as any other components.

Do not use several programs to express one behavior that should be a single model. Split only when the pieces have genuinely different clocks, languages, or ownership.

docs.title: Deleting a program
docs.text:
Deleting the child prim removes the behavior. Deleting the owning prim removes the program with it. There is no separate "stop script" registry to clean up.

If a program acquired control, its stop hook runs during removal. A program that fails to release control leaves the runtime in a visible held state rather than silently continuing with stale authority.

docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Put the program under the object it controls.
  • Prefer sourceAsset over inline sourceCode.
  • Declare realtimeSafe only when the program can meet the budget.
  • Match the prim's inputs: and outputs: to the compiled interface.
  • Release control and stop actuators in the stop hook.
  • Treat a source reload as a replacement, not as a mutation of the old program.

Continue with Materials, which bind appearance to the same composed prims.
